currentUse: Active diocesan Lithuanian Catholic parish; Lithuanian-language Masses Sundays and Fridays, English Mass Saturdays
summary: Divine Providence is the sole surviving Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish institution in metropolitan Detroit. Formed in 1949 from the St. George parish community while St. George itself remained active, it first worshipped in the Divine Providence church on Schaefer Road in Detroit. That church was demolished in November 1970 for freeway construction; the same parish institution moved to Southfield, where its present church and cultural center were dedicated on September 8, 1973. St. Anthony Lithuanian Parish merged into Divine Providence in 2013. The parish remains active with weekly Lithuanian worship. It is included in the Archdiocese of Detroit's Planning Area 8 restructuring process, but no merger, closure, or final pastorate decision has been made.
historicalSummary: Divine Providence grew from Detroit's first Lithuanian Catholic parish, St. George. On July 25, 1948, about 100 St. George parishioners broke ground for a new Lithuanian church south of Grand River on Schaefer. Because the original St. George parish and church still remained active, the chancery would not allow the name to be reused; the new parish institution was named Divine Providence.

The Schaefer church's cornerstone was blessed on March 6, 1949, and the completed church was blessed that December. St. George remained a distinct parish through 1965, and its Westminster church was demolished for the Chrysler Freeway in 1966. Divine Providence then faced a second displacement when the Jeffries Freeway took the Schaefer site.

The last Mass on Schaefer was celebrated May 17, 1970. Beginning May 24, the parish worshipped temporarily at St. Beatrice in Southfield while building its permanent home. The Schaefer church was demolished in November 1970; the present Divine Providence church and cultural center on Nine Mile Road were dedicated September 8, 1973.

developments.detail: Detroit Catholic reported 156 sessions at 78 parishes completed, further waves beginning May 20 and June 17, and an online survey accepting feedback on the models through July 31, 2026.

developments.headline: Named among parishes that could lose weekend Mass
developments.detail: Detroit News reported that Divine Providence could stop holding weekend Mass under at least one proposed restructuring model; current Archdiocese materials place the parish in Planning Area 8 and state that no final decision has been made.

developments.headline: Public feedback window closes
developments.detail: The Archdiocese of Detroit's Listening Session Feedback Survey closed on July 31, 2026 — the restructuring site now reads 'The Post-Listening Session Survey is Now Closed.' Divine Providence remains an active Lithuanian personal parish in Planning Area 8 while the three draft pastorate models are refined (Phase 2, through December 2026). Per the Archdiocese's published timeline, Archbishop Weisenburger announces pastorate decisions in Phase 3, January-June 2027, with implementation beginning July 2027; no final decision has been made.
